request.spec:
The sheet has a rate for each grade: a percent with two decimals, set on the screen (RATE_SET
grade=<grade> rate=<rate> in the audit). A claim's due is its amount times the rate for its
person's grade, divided by 100, rounded half up to two decimals (a half rounds away from zero:
1.025 becomes 1.03). Show due on each claim. Show each person's due-total: their claimed times
their grade's rate, divided by 100, rounded the same way. Show the sheet's due-total: everyone's
due-total added up. A grade with no rate makes its claims' due and its people's due-total n/a,
and a total skips n/a.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has a rate for each grade: a percent with two decimals, set on the screen (RATE_SET
grade=<grade> rate=<rate> in the audit). A claim's due is its amount times the rate for its
person's grade, divided by 100, rounded half up to two decimals (a half rounds away from zero:
1.025 becomes 1.03). Show due on each claim. Show each person's due-total: their claimed times
their grade's rate, divided by 100, rounded the same way. Show the sheet's due-total: everyone's
due-total added up. A grade with no rate makes its claims' due and its people's due-total n/a,
and a total skips n/a.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added grade rates and due amounts to the sheet, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**What you see on screen**
- A new **Rates** section has a form where you pick a grade and type a percent, and a table showing each grade's current rate (`n/a` if it has none).
- Each claim shows its **due**: amount × rate ÷ 100, rounded half up to two decimals.
- Each person shows a **due-total**: their claimed total × their grade's rate ÷ 100, rounded the same way. This is not the sum of their claims' dues. Two claims of 10.25 at 10% are due 1.03 each, but the person's due-total is 2.05.
- The sheet shows **Due in total**, which adds up everyone's due-total and skips any that are `n/a`.

**Stored data and server**
- A new migration, `V6__rate.sql`, adds a `rate` table with one rate per grade per sheet.
- A new `rate` package on the server lists a sheet's rates and sets one grade's rate. Setting a grade that already has a rate replaces it.
- Every successful set writes `RATE_SET sheet=<id> by=<user> grade=<grade> rate=<rate>` to the audit file, even when the rate doesn't change. The tests expect that line when a rate is set again to the value it already has.

**Front end**
- The Rates section is a new component in `rates.ts`. The people list now loads the rates along with people and claims, so they re-read whenever the sheet is reloaded.
- Due is worked out in the browser in whole cents and hundredths of a percent, so the sums are exact.

The request didn't set limits on a rate. I chose to accept any percent of 0.00 or more with up to two decimals and at most five whole digits. A rate in any other form shows the error and saves nothing.
